description: Escape vendor lock-in. Learn to run powerful open-source AI models locally using the Hugging Face transformers library, and explore fine-tuning techniques like LoRA.

slides.title: The Open Source AI Revolution
slides.content:
# Beyond OpenAI 🌍

Using OpenAI's API is easy, but it has downsides:
1. **Privacy:** You are sending your data to a 3rd party.
2. **Cost:** API calls get expensive at scale.
3. **Control:** OpenAI can change or deprecate models at any time.

The alternative is **Open-Source AI**. You download the model files to your own server and run them locally. 

The central hub for open-source AI is **Hugging Face**.

slides.title: The transformers Library
slides.content:
# Downloading Models 🤗

Hugging Face provides the `transformers` Python library, which makes downloading and running state-of-the-art models (like Meta's Llama 3 or Mistral) incredibly simple.

```bash
# Install transformers and PyTorch (the underlying math engine)
pip install transformers torch
```

```python_not
from transformers import pipeline

# The pipeline is the highest-level API
# It automatically downloads the model and handles all the complex math
classifier = pipeline("sentiment-analysis")

result = classifier("I absolutely love Python programming!")
print(result) 
# Output: [{'label': 'POSITIVE', 'score': 0.9998}]
```

slides.title: AutoClasses
slides.content:
# Under the Hood: Tokenizers 🧩

The `pipeline` is great for quick tasks, but for deep control, we use `AutoClasses`.

AI models cannot read text; they only understand numbers. 

A **Tokenizer** splits text into sub-words (tokens) and converts them into IDs. You *must* use the exact tokenizer that was used to train the model!

```python_not
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

model_id = "gpt2" # A small, open-source language model

# Download and load the specific tokenizer for GPT-2
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)

# Download and load the model itself
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id)

# Convert text into a tensor (multi-dimensional array) of numbers
inputs = tokenizer("The capital of France is", return_tensors="pt")
```

slides.title: Generating Text Locally
slides.content:
# Running the Model 💻

Once we have the tokenized input, we pass it to the model to generate the next tokens, and then decode the numerical output back into human-readable text.

```python_not
# (Continuing from previous slide)

# Generate text (max 20 new tokens)
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=20)

# Decode the output numbers back into a string
text = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

print(text)
# Output: The capital of France is Paris. It is the most populous city in...
```

> 💡 **Note:** Running large models (like Llama-3-8B) requires a powerful GPU and lots of VRAM. Without a GPU, generation will be incredibly slow.

slides.content: Check your understanding of the Hugging Face ecosystem.
slides.quizQuestion: In the `transformers` library, what is the critical role of a Tokenizer?
quizOptions: It authenticates your API key with Hugging Face.
It translates Python code into C++ for faster execution.

slides.title: Introduction to Fine-Tuning
slides.content:
# Teaching New Tricks 🎓

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is great for giving an AI new *knowledge* (facts).

**Fine-Tuning** is used to give an AI new *skills* or change its *behavior*. 

For example, if you want a model to consistently output valid Python code formatted exactly to your company's highly specific internal style guide, RAG will struggle. You need to Fine-Tune the model by showing it thousands of examples of your code.

slides.title: The Cost of Fine-Tuning
slides.content:
# Full Fine-Tuning vs PEFT 💰

A large model like Llama-3-8B has 8 billion parameters (mathematical weights).

Historically, fine-tuning meant updating *all* 8 billion parameters simultaneously. This required massive server clusters and hundreds of thousands of dollars.

This led to the invention of **PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning)**.

slides.title: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
slides.content:
# The LoRA Revolution 🔬

**LoRA** is the most popular PEFT technique.

Instead of updating the 8 billion original parameters, LoRA freezes the entire base model. It then injects a tiny, "low-rank" matrix (e.g., just 10 million parameters) next to the base model.

During training, *only* the tiny matrix is updated! 

This reduces memory requirements by 90%, allowing you to fine-tune massive AI models on a single consumer GPU in a few hours!

slides.title: Using the SFTTrainer
slides.content:
# Code: Supervised Fine-Tuning 🏋️

Hugging Face provides the `SFTTrainer` (Supervised Fine-Tuning Trainer) via the `trl` library to make fine-tuning with LoRA easy.

```python_not
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from trl import SFTTrainer

# 1. Define the LoRA configuration (the tiny matrices)
lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=8, # Rank (size of the tiny matrix)
    target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], # Inject into attention layers
    task_type="CAUSAL_LM"
)

# 2. Wrap the base model with the LoRA config
peft_model = get_peft_model(base_model, lora_config)

# 3. Initialize the Trainer
trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=peft_model,
    train_dataset=my_custom_dataset,
    dataset_text_field="text",
)

# 4. Train the model!
trainer.train()
```

slides.title: Fine-Tuning Quiz
slides.content: Ensure you know when and how to train.
slides.quizQuestion: Why is LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) used when fine-tuning massive Language Models?
quizOptions: It connects the model to the internet.
It freezes the massive base model and only trains a tiny injected matrix, drastically reducing the required GPU memory and compute time.
It converts the model into a Vector Database.
It automatically downloads data from Wikipedia to train the model.

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Open Source AI Developer! 🎉

You've learned how to harness models locally without relying on paid APIs.

## Key Takeaways

- ✅ **Hugging Face:** The central repository for open-source AI models and datasets.
- ✅ **transformers:** Use `pipeline()` for rapid deployment, or `AutoModel` and `AutoTokenizer` for deep control.
- ✅ **Tokenization:** AI only understands numbers. You must map text to numerical IDs using the model's specific Tokenizer.
- ✅ **RAG vs Fine-Tuning:** Use RAG to add facts/knowledge. Use Fine-Tuning to change the model's behavior/skills/format.
- ✅ **LoRA / PEFT:** Never do full fine-tuning. Use LoRA to train a tiny "adapter" matrix alongside a frozen base model, allowing training on standard GPUs.
